🎯 1. PHQ-9 Depression Severity Profile

The Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) is the primary clinical diagnostic standard in this dataset. PHQ-9 scores range from 0 to 27 and map to five standard clinical categories:

Category PHQ-9 Range Count Percentage
0: None / Minimal0 - 44,02437.0%
1: Mild5 - 93,26730.1%
2: Moderate10 - 141,98018.2%
3: Moderately Severe15 - 191,0549.7%
4: Severe20 - 275415.0%
Key Takeaway: Mild-to-moderate depression is prevalent (48.3%), while severe depression represents a critical 5.0% minority class requiring specialized focal weighting in ML models.

🏃 2. Actigraphy & Sleep Digital Biomarkers

Sensor metrics captured from wearable accelerometers reveal profound behavioral alterations associated with depression:

  • Daily Step Count: Non-depressed subjects log ~9,463 awake steps daily. This decreases linearly to ~6,980 steps daily in severe depression.
  • Sleep Efficiency & In-Bed Time: While total sleep duration stays at ~6 hours across all categories, severely depressed individuals remain in bed 34 minutes longer per night without sleeping, yielding an efficiency drop from 90.9% to 84.8%.
  • Sleep Schedule Variability: Sleep duration IQR increases by 31.2% (96.2 min to 126.1 min), reflecting severe circadian rhythm instability.

🔄 4. State Transitions & Clinical Comorbidities

Clinical Comorbidity Insight: Participants with comorbid migraines or chronic neuropathic pain display average PHQ-9 scores over double those without these conditions (e.g. 12.1 vs 5.8 for neuropathic pain).

💡 5. Machine Learning Modeling Recommendations

1. Group-Based Cross Validation

Always use GroupKFold(groups=user_id) to split data. Random row splitting will leak participant baseline data and severely overfit.

2. Feature Interaction Ratios

Create features such as steps_awake_mean / sleep_in_bed_weekday_mean to capture activity vs rest imbalance.

3. Imbalanced Class Loss

Apply class weights or focal loss to account for Severe (5.0%) and Moderately Severe (9.7%) minority classes.
